speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. speaker: Doctor
text: Given the history of fractures and bone fragility, I need to assess for other systemic symptoms. Have you experienced any hearing loss, vision problems, or unusual skin changes like easy bruising? REQUEST TEST: Bone_Density_Scan

speaker: Doctor
text: Let's look at your physical development. Have you noticed any excess hair growth on your face, chest, or back, and do you have a deepened voice or enlarged clitoris? REQUEST TEST: Serum_Testosterone_and_LH_FSH

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the combination of ambiguous genitalia at birth, maternal virilization, and primary amenorrhea, I suspect a disorder of sexual development like Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia. REQUEST TEST: 17-Hydroxyprogesterone_and_Cortisol

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated 17-hydroxyprogesterone and low cortisol strongly suggest Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia, likely due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency. speaker: Doctor
text: Wait, the elevated 11-deoxycortisol actually points to 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency rather than 21-hydroxylase deficiency, which explains the hypertension and virilization. Do you have a history of high blood pressure or headaches? DIAGNOSIS READY: 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency
